title: Asset size threshold and regulatory burden on bank profitability

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) using the $10B asset threshold. The key assumption is that banks cannot precisely manipulate their assets around the cutoff, creating quasi-random assignment to regulatory treatment. However, the concern about strategic asset management suggests potential manipulation, making this a fuzzy RDD where we need to test for discontinuities in the running variable density and use robust bandwidth selection.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s28_data.csv")

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0.5)
print("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===")
print(summary(rdd_result))

# Extract key coefficient
treatment_effect <- rdd_result$coef[1]
cat("\nTreatment Effect (Local Average Treatment Effect):", round(treatment_effect, 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(rdd_result$se[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_result$pv[1], 4), "\n")

# Robustness checks
print("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===")

# 1. Test for manipulation (McCrary density test)
density_test <- rddensity(data$running_var, c = 0.5)
print("Density Test (manipulation check):")
print(density_test)

# 2. Alternative bandwidth
rdd_alt_bw <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0.5, 
                       h = rdd_result$bws[1,1] * 0.8)
print("\nAlternative bandwidth (80% of optimal):")
print(summary(rdd_alt_bw))

# 3. Different polynomial orders
rdd_quad <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0.5, p = 2)
print("\nQuadratic specification:")
print(summary(rdd_quad))

# 4. Subset analysis for near-cutoff observations
near_cutoff_data <- data[data$near_cutoff == 1, ]
if(nrow(near_cutoff_data) > 50) {
  rdd_near <- rdrobust(y = near_cutoff_data$y, x = near_cutoff_data$running_var, c = 0.5)
  print("\nNear-cutoff subsample analysis:")
  print(summary(rdd_near))
}

# Create visualization
plot_data <- data[abs(data$running_var - 0.5) <= 0.3, ]  # Focus around cutoff
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = running_var, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, aes(color = factor(treated))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(data = plot_data[plot_data$running_var < 0.5, ], 
              method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(data = plot_data[plot_data$running_var > 0.5, ], 
              method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "RDD: Bank Profitability at $10B Asset Threshold",
       x = "Running Variable (Centered Log Assets)",
       y = "ROA",
       color = "Treated") +
  theme_minimal()

# Summary statistics
print("\n=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===")
print("Overall sample:")
print(summary(data))
print("\nBy treatment status:")
print(by(data[c("y", "running_var")], data$treated, summary))

# Final result
cat("\n=== FINAL RESULT ===")
cat("The estimated effect of crossing the $10B threshold on ROA is:", 
    round(treatment_effect, 4), "\n")
if(abs(rdd_result$pv[1]) < 0.05) {
  cat("This effect is statistically significant at the 5% level.\n")
} else {
  cat("This effect is not statistically significant at the 5% level.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a negative treatment effect of approximately -0.02 to -0.05 (2-5 percentage points reduction in ROA). The additional regulatory burden from Dodd-Frank requirements for banks over $10B (enhanced supervision, stress testing, liquidity requirements) should increase compliance costs and reduce operational efficiency, thereby lowering profitability. The magnitude reflects the substantial regulatory costs while recognizing that large banks may have some economies of scale that partially offset these burdens.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — asset threshold; test for bunching below $10B; local linear regression
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Banks just above threshold have lower ROA than just-below peers
